title: Frustration without Glass in Non-Abelian Simplicial Networks
abstract: We formulate a non-Abelian theory of structural consistency for systems in which dynamical transformations reside on the links of a simplicial network. Gauge covariance follows from freedom to choose local representation frames, while plaquette holonomies quantify the incompatibility of alternative paths. For an SU(2) model on the complete simplicial $2$-complex with quenched random plaquette couplings, parallel-tempering simulations reveal a continuous disorder-driven loss of global compatibility. In the high-disorder phase, the uniform compatibility $M_P$ decreases with system size, the integrated adjacent correlation weight $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{adj}}$ remains finite value. Moreover, the connected replica-overlap width approaches the numerical noise floor and its distribution narrows, providing no evidence for thermodynamic replica-symmetry breaking. Dense frustration therefore produces a non-glassy correlated gauge liquid in which individual pair correlations are geometrically diluted while a finite integrated correlation weight survives.
summary: This work analyzes a non-Abelian gauge network subjected to quenched frustration, modeling structural consistency via plaquette holonomies. By analyzing key correlation measures, the authors demonstrate that the system enters a non-glassy correlated liquid phase rather than freezing into a spin-glass state. This suggests that collective order can persist through geometric dilution of local correlations.
main_problem: The paper investigates the collective phase that emerges in systems with non-Abelian holonomies when subjected to quenched, mutually frustrating couplings, aiming to distinguish this from conventional glassy freezing.
main_result: Dense frustration leads to a non-glassy correlated gauge liquid, characterized by a finite integrated correlation weight despite the geometric dilution of individual pair correlations.
method: The study employs theoretical formulation of non-Abelian gauge networks and utilizes advanced numerical techniques like parallel-tempering simulations and replica overlap analysis.
model_or_system: The model is a non-Abelian gauge network defined on an oriented simplicial 2-complex, where link transformations belong to a group like SU(2). The dynamics are governed by a Hamiltonian involving Wilson plaquette observables with quenched random couplings.
key_observables: Global compatibility ($m_P$), connected adjacent correlation weight ($I_{	ext{adj}}$), and connected replica-overlap width ($W_c$).
important_parameters: High-disorder phase, quenched random couplings ($J_f$), and the system size ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the SU(2) model on the complete simplicial 2-complex, and the interpretation relies on distinguishing between different types of correlation decay.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the continuous disorder-driven loss of global compatibility, the finite nature of $I_{	ext{adj}}$ in the high-disorder phase, and the vanishing of replica overlap width, confirming the non-glassy liquid state.
paper_structure: The paper builds by defining the gauge network and Hamiltonian, then analyzing the behavior of key observables ($m_P, I_{	ext{adj}}, W_c$) across different disorder regimes to rule out glassy freezing and establish the correlated liquid phase.
why_interesting: The concept of a 'correlated gauge liquid' provides a novel theoretical framework for understanding collective organization in highly frustrated systems, moving beyond standard spin-glass paradigms.

(b) Binder cumulant U4, showing a common crossing within the window ∆c ≃0.44 ± 0.01. (c) Connected thermal susceptibility of the plaquettes χP,con, whose maximum grows and peak width shrinks with the system size. Error bars represent disorder-resolved statistical uncertainties.
